title: Actual-relation descent and the normal-three center
scope: Work over the fixed original finite extension K/Q_p with its original absolute value, on good, Hausdorff, boundaryless quasi-smooth spaces and ordinary opens. Scalars have the specified finite continuous admissible PL/PS presentations, including full delta curvature and all closed-cell face data. Allowed backgrounds are symmetric, middle-positive and separately closed, in the displayed legal degree. All original compact smooth CLD tests and actual refinements are retained. A proved conditional implication does not establish its open premise; source status is not new independent proof acceptance.

nodes.title: Quadratic transgression and first derivatives
nodes.summary: For a finite admissible quadratic presentation P, the full degree-one action obeys A_S(P) = D M_S(α_P) = −D M_S(Z_P). The singular term A₀ = ½Dδ(Σcνhνkν) is retained. Full first derivatives commute with M_S, including polyhedral boundary contributions.

nodes.title: An actual full-exact certificate
nodes.summary: On one ordinary representative chosen for P, α_P = d′β + d″ζ in the actual delta-form sheaf. This is a hypothesis available in proved special cases; its existence for every quadratic actual zero remains open. It does not require a continuous smooth-form double primitive.

nodes.title: Exact approximants with one control
nodes.summary: Actual symmetric full-exact forms a_j approximate α_P in the represented order interval −ε_jQ ≤ [α_P]−[a_j] ≤ ε_jQ, with ε_j → 0 and one fixed positive represented Q. The all-background degree-one estimate is part of this certificate. The same ordinary domain, Q and approximants precede later backgrounds, tests and refinements.

nodes.title: A zero full-carrier seminorm
nodes.summary: For the specified closed carrier F, the unchanged carrier-CLN seminorm of P vanishes at every required enlarged compact stage. Only the permitted harmonic, pointwise-zero-product and ambient-cycle generators are used. Whether every actual PL-zero has the required absolute-cap certificates is open; zero action does not imply this stronger certificate.

nodes.title: The specified quadratic action vanishes
nodes.summary: The action A_S(P) is zero on all original compact smooth complementary tests under any one incoming sufficient route and that route’s displayed hypotheses. Exactness and fixed-control approximation allow every legal S. The direct carrier theorem allows the S carried by its specified F. This node does not assert that every actual relation already has such a certificate.

links.label: Carrier implication with its support condition

nodes.title: Rank at most two constructs certificates
nodes.summary: For an actual quadratic zero in a fixed finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS presentation with joint residue rank s_f(x) ≤ 2, the source construction returns a full strain covector to the whole actual moment image. It constructs both full first-order exactness and fixed-Q approximants on an ordinary neighborhood, in arbitrary ambient dimension.

nodes.title: A canonical quotient when s_K ≤ 2
nodes.summary: If the entire residue dimension satisfies s_K(x) ≤ 2, the quadratic transgression class depends only on the actual quadratic curvature. The canonical map τ₂ satisfies D̄τ₂ = id. These classes glue on ordinary opens satisfying the bound, including analytic surfaces. Separately low-rank presentations are insufficient unless their union tuple also meets the bound.

nodes.title: Descent over weakly approximable backgrounds
nodes.summary: For S in W_loc, actual delta-form action is presentation independent, local and compatible with full first derivatives. W_loc uses weak convergence on all original smooth tests on one fixed ordinary domain, allowing nets. Fixed continuous curvature slots preserve the required weak convergence; bounded BT tails remain in the class.

nodes.title: Every allowed background lies in W_loc
nodes.summary: The proposed density theorem would put each arbitrary symmetric middle-positive, separately closed original background in the same-domain weak closure of actual positive closed delta-form backgrounds. Existing potential, cap and geometric examples do not establish this assertion for an arbitrary current.

links.label: What the available approximation route requires

nodes.title: General actual-relation descent
nodes.summary: For every admissible finite actual curvature relation of every degree b, choose an ordinary representative for the relation before S and tests, and prove A_S(P) = 0 for all legal backgrounds and all actual refinements. The general quadratic case remains open; low-rank and supplied-model conclusions retain their hypotheses.

nodes.title: Higher and coefficient interfaces
nodes.summary: A general differential calculus still needs presentation independence for variable finite PS coefficients and higher coupled tails, the differential identities, the intended delta-test extension, and gluing and naturality in the stated mapping class. One common BT tail can be absorbed into S; different termwise tails cannot be absorbed by that argument.

nodes.title: A supplied normal-three actual zero
nodes.summary: A supplied smooth integral normal-three model germ (Y,y) over the original field, with unchanged value group and residue transcendence degree three, carries the fixed finite closed-cell PL/PS quadratic actual zero. The supplied data include original-field lifting, complete-source comparison on a smooth projective SNC model, all labelled Gauss families and lower strata, and ordinary convergence uniform in the angular parameter.

links.label: Actual quadratic relation and supplied source hypotheses

nodes.title: Action vanishes off the center
nodes.summary: In that supplied model, an ordinary U chosen for P before S and tests satisfies A_S(P)|_(U minus {y}) = 0. The proof covers actual ordinary points through top-cone neighborhoods, marked-curve tubes, completed surface core fibers and the rank-two complement. It uses current locality, not a single global primitive on the puncture.

nodes.title: Only a top-degree Dirac remains
nodes.summary: The finite signed BT action is coefficient-Radon and separately closed. In the supplied threefold, punctured vanishing therefore gives zero everywhere for p = 0, and A_S(P) = c_S(P) δ_y for p = 1. The scalar is independent of the compact cutoff equal to one near y.

nodes.title: Protected tangents retain the wall terms
nodes.summary: For the same degree-one S and a protected actual presentation, the full-fiber transpose T has critical trace mass O(r²) and positive closed conic tangent limits T₀. The paired leading PL energy Z₀ satisfies an all-face O(r) error estimate. Compatible-PS continuity retains wall mass when passing its pairing to a tangent; ordinary smooth weak convergence alone would not suffice.

nodes.title: An exact spherical residual formula
nodes.summary: For every critical tangent jointly realized by this P and S, c_S(P) equals Σcν(∫hν^[1]kν^[1] dσ − ∫d_S hν^[1] ⊗ d_S kν^[1] : dM). The finite positive semidefinite angular matrix measure satisfies Mθ = 0, div_S M = 0 and σ = tr M. The value is tangent independent. Classification of real cones does not show that an arbitrary real cone is analytically realized.

links.label: Real classification and its realization boundary

nodes.title: The realized spherical pairing vanishes
nodes.summary: The missing assertion is cancellation for every actual jointly realized pair (Z₀,M) in this supplied-model category. It is known for zero tangent density, globally linear first jets, and a leading tensor with an actual full-exact identity near the whole protected central fiber; the established potential and W_loc subclasses are also covered. No argument yet covers all allowed S and all actual zero relations.

nodes.title: Full quadratic descent in this model
nodes.summary: If the open cancellation assertion is proved throughout the supplied normal-three class, its quadratic actual zeros have zero action on U in both legal degrees p = 0 and p = 1. This is a specific conditional target. It neither returns the model to every original germ nor settles higher coupled or variable-coefficient relations.

links.label: Already proved punctured and lower-degree cases

nodes.title: Why shortcut arguments stop
nodes.summary: Normal-current constructions retain a harmonic boundary defect; scalar harmonic identifications do not supply a missing continuous potential. N07 excludes an automatic continuous smooth-form double primitive. N08 gives a real Killing-gluing obstruction, N09 retains graph Hessian-wall drift, N10 obstructs stronger residue-section and whole-central-fiber Hensel lifts, and N11 shows that O(r²) growth can retain a point residual. These examples do not refute the actual analytic-zero conjecture.

A continuous potential is an input

N11: critical mass does not force removal

hypotheses: P is the specified admissible finite quadratic actual zero on the same ordinary representative as its full-exact identity.
S is any allowed original background of degree 0 ≤ p ≤ n−2; retain all original compact smooth tests and actual refinements.
relations.explanation: Full derivative compatibility gives M_S(α_P) = d′(β ∧ S) + d″(ζ ∧ S). Applying D kills both terms by nilpotence and anticommutation. No higher-degree arbitrary-current product is assumed.

hypotheses: P is the specified admissible finite quadratic actual zero, with exact a_j, ε_j → 0 and a single positive represented Q on one fixed ordinary neighborhood.
The represented order estimate transfers to the all-background degree-one action for every allowed 0 ≤ p ≤ n−2; Q and the neighborhood do not vary with the test or later refinement.
relations.explanation: Each exact a_j has zero differentiated action. The fixed positive control bounds every remaining compact pairing by ε_j times a finite fixed mass; distributional continuity of D then gives zero. Approximating only Z_P retains the complete singular A₀ term.

hypotheses: Here P is a finite quadratic PL curvature polynomial and S is an allowed background carried by the specified unchanged closed F, in a legal degree.
Zero seminorm holds at every enlarged compact stage required for the test, using finite decompositions on the same ordinary domain and only the permitted generator space.

An absolute-cap certificate directly kills its relative capped background. Returning from all such caps to an uncapped S uses the separate KC9 detector: q = n−(p+b) > 0 and 1 ≤ c ≤ max(q mod 2, q−2 floor(p/2)). That proposition gives no positive-rank cap route when q = 0 or this upper bound is zero.
relations.explanation: Permitted carrier relations act by zero. Apply the uniform carrier-only CLN estimate to each remainder and take the seminorm infimum. This proves a sufficient annihilation criterion; it does not identify the actual analytic kernel or all seminorm polars.

hypotheses: The fixed relation is an actual quadratic zero in the finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS class, and its entire original scalar tuple f satisfies s_f(x) ≤ 2.
Use the constructed ordinary neighborhood and finite actual original-unit refinement; all lower strata and later deficient-rank refinements remain included.
relations.explanation: The normal-surface construction returns a continuous finite-PS covector whose full strain is Z_P on the whole actual moment image. Since A₀ = ½Dδu is already full-exact, α_P = A₀−Z_P has an actual first-order exact expression.

hypotheses: Retain the same actual zero, full finite closed-cell source data and joint bound s_f(x) ≤ 2.
Fix 1 < κ < 2 and one ordinary truncation before later backgrounds and tests.
relations.explanation: Regularize the returned continuous covector and use the finitely many coefficient facets, |ℓ_H|^κ and a fixed strictly convex term to construct one positive Q = D[q]. The source-side all-background estimate is O(δ^((2−κ)/2)); setting a_j = A₀−e_δj yields the required full-exact approximation.

hypotheses: Impose the stronger intrinsic bound s_K(x) ≤ 2, so the union tuple of any two finite presentations has joint residue rank at most two.
For a sheaf morphism, this bound holds at every point of the ordinary open; local finite presentations and the actual quotient sheaf are retained.
relations.explanation: Two presentations of one actual quadratic curvature differ by an actual zero. Apply rank-two exactness to their union tuple, so their transgression classes agree. The singular A₀ is exact, and ordinary sheaf gluing gives τ₂ with D̄τ₂ = id. Separate rank bounds on the two tuples alone would not justify this argument.

hypotheses: Retain every supplied original-field model/source comparison, labelled cone, calibration and completed core fiber in the model hypothesis.
P is the fixed admissible quadratic actual zero; S is any allowed original background with p = 0 or p = 1 on the supplied threefold.
Choose the ordinary U for P before S and compact tests; the cover is a cover of actual ordinary points.
relations.explanation: Top interiors have ambient strain neighborhoods, positive two-faces use completed marked-curve data, and rays use ordinary neighborhoods of completed surface core fibers. Outside the fixed old source, the original scalar tuple has rank at most two. A finite partition of each compact test and ordinary current locality assemble the punctured equality.

hypotheses: The current is the finite signed bounded BT action of the specified continuous PL/PS quadratic presentation, so it is coefficient-Radon and separately d′- and d″-closed.
The ambient analytic dimension is three and p is 0 or 1.
relations.explanation: Punctured vanishing puts the support at y. A separately closed order-zero point current vanishes below top bidegree; in top degree it is a scalar Dirac measure. Thus p = 0 is complete, while p = 1 has precisely c_S(P)δ_y left.

links.label: PA9: its application to the signed BT action

hypotheses: Use the same actual quadratic presentation and an allowed degree-one background S.
Supply a finite protected actual moment map t containing every scalar, with t(y) = 0 and the whole inverse image of every compact target support compact in U.
Retain the complete finite closed-cell scalar jets and their tangential values on every face.
relations.explanation: Transposing original tests through the protected whole fiber gives a positive separately closed real current. The critical monotonicity estimate supplies conic tangent subsequences; the paired first-jet estimate gives O(r) coefficient error, and the compatible-PS approximation controls the wall terms for the tangent pairing.

hypotheses: The residual, transpose, leading tensor and tangent come from the same P, S and protected actual presentation; take p = 1.
Use the full paired tensor Z₀ and canonical tangential face values, with the complete protected inverse image retained in every shrinking cutoff.
relations.explanation: A cutoff Hessian has size O(δ⁻²), while trace mass is O(δ²) and the leading-energy error is O(δ), so the replacement error tends to zero. Compatible-PS continuity passes the remaining pairing to T₀. Radial and tangential decomposition then gives the spherical formula and D(Z₀ ∧ T₀) = −c_S(P)δ₀.

hypotheses: Assume the still-open cancellation statement for every admissible quadratic actual zero and every degree-one S in this supplied-model category, with their common protected presentations.
Retain the already proved p = 0 case and punctured vanishing from the point-residual theorem.
relations.explanation: The formula identifies the only remaining coefficient c_S(P) with the hypothesized zero pairing. This removes the central Dirac in degree p = 1; the degree p = 0 action already vanishes. The implication is proved, but its universal cancellation premise remains open.

links.label: Critical cancellation and the precise remaining case

hypotheses: The shortcut under examination uses local strain primitives, graph pullback or critical O(r²) mass alone, without additional actual-zero realization data.
The real Killing example is not separately closed; the critical-mass example is not an actual analytic-zero presentation. Their counterexamples have precisely these restricted targets.
relations.explanation: Local primitives can fail to glue, pulling a primitive through a PL graph retains a Hessian-wall measure, and O(r²) mass can survive a second-order cutoff. In the analytic cancellation problem the available ε⁻¹ times O(ε) wall bound is only O(1). These results block those shortcuts, while leaving cancellation for jointly realized actual zero pairs open.

hypotheses: Assume the open density statement for every allowed background in every legal degree on fixed ordinary representatives, with convergence against all original compact smooth tests.
Keep the admissible finite continuous PL/PS scalar presentation fixed while the positive separately closed backgrounds vary; apply the established fixed-slot and compatible-PS continuity.
relations.explanation: For actual delta-form backgrounds the zero relation has zero product. On a fixed local domain, pass each term of the finite expression through the established weak-continuity theorem. This kills actual zero presentations for S; subtracting presentations and ordinary locality give descent. This route does not require an exactness certificate for each relation.

hypotheses: A new return theorem must cover arbitrary original ordinary germs, including higher joint residue rank and model data not supplied in advance.
Higher degrees need treatment of coupled relations with different termwise tails; a common-tail absorption argument only treats its stated subclass.
Preserve the original field, all original tests and actual refinements, and choose the ordinary relation neighborhood before S and tests.
relations.explanation: Even complete cancellation would settle the quadratic supplied normal-three case. These missing general-germ and higher-degree bridges are additional research tasks; no implication from that model theorem alone to REL-ALL is claimed.

links.label: Why common tails leave coupled relations open

hypotheses: Even after pure scalar relation descent, specify and prove the variable-coefficient quotient and the differential identities in their object sheaves.
Establish the intended enlarged delta-test action, ordinary gluing and naturality for an explicit mapping class; equality on smooth tests alone does not define that extension.
relations.explanation: Scalar descent would make its curvature expressions presentation independent. Variable PS coefficients, differential operations and enlarged tests ask for separate compatibility statements, so neither low-rank descent nor central cancellation supplies this interface automatically.

hypotheses: The proposed shortcut strengthens finite original-unit lifting into a relation-preserving residue-field section, or extends a selected Hensel logarithm continuously over the entire central moment image.
The cited obstructions concern these stronger constructions, not every possible route to actual-relation descent.
relations.explanation: The residue-field example has no rational coefficient-field section and even a displayed pair of units cannot lift with its prescribed equation. The Hensel example has two approaching branches with incompatible limiting norms after any finite unit refinement. A general return theorem must respect these failures rather than assume those stronger lifts.

panels.title: Three sufficient routes, with a rank-two construction
panels.summary: Each incoming route can make the specified quadratic action vanish. Multiple incoming relations are alternatives (OR); the inputs inside a single relation are joint requirements (AND). Rank two constructs the two transgression certificates, while the canonical quotient additionally needs control of the union tuple.

panels.title: From a supplied actual zero to the unresolved central coefficient
panels.summary: Punctured vanishing leaves only a top-degree Dirac. The point-residual theorem AND the protected tangent estimates identify its coefficient. Full model descent then needs the still-open cancellation assertion; shortcut counterexamples are not counterexamples to that assertion.

panels.title: What would reach the general conjecture?
panels.summary: The established W_loc calculus AND a new density theorem would give the all-background route. Extending a solved model case to arbitrary germs and higher coupled relations remains a separate open step. Variable coefficients and enlarged differential interfaces remain separate tasks after scalar descent.
